name: Banyan Tree Bangkok
short_description: A 327-room, 5-star all-suite tower in Bangkok's Sathorn CBD, home to the 61st-floor Vertigo rooftop restaurant and Moon Bar.
ai_summary: Banyan Tree Bangkok is a five-star hotel occupying a slim, 61-story tower in the Sathorn Central Business District, open since January 2002 and long recognized as one of Bangkok's tallest luxury hotels. Its 327 rooms and suites -- Horizon, Skyline, Panorama Club and Vertigo Club categories, plus multi-bedroom Serenity and Presidential Suites -- sit on floors 15 through 58, with city or Lumphini Park views from floor-to-ceiling windows. The hotel is best known for Vertigo, its open-air rooftop grill restaurant, and Moon Bar next door, both on a converted helipad with 360-degree skyline views; a rooftop pool and full spa round out the facilities. Guest and travel-writer reviews consistently praise the views, spa, dining and attentive service, while a recurring critique is that the lobby, some public areas and the modestly sized rooftop pool show their age relative to newer Bangkok luxury openings.

pros: 327 all-suite-style rooms in a landmark 61-story Sathorn tower, open since 2002
Vertigo rooftop restaurant and Moon Bar on the 61st floor deliver genuine 360-degree Bangkok skyline views
Club Lounge access for eligible room categories includes breakfast, afternoon tea and evening cocktails
Central Sathorn CBD location near Lumphini Park, Chao Phraya river piers, and Siam/CentralWorld shopping
Comprehensive spa built around Banyan Tree's wellbeing programming
cons: Lobby and some public areas read as dated next to newer Bangkok luxury openings, per multiple 2024-2025 reviews
The 21st-floor rooftop pool is small and can feel undersized for the hotel's scale
research_highlights: Multiple independent reviews single out Vertigo and Moon Bar as a genuine landmark Bangkok experience, not just a hotel amenity
Reviewers repeatedly describe the hotel as strong value for a 5-star suite-only property given typical nightly rates
Club Lounge benefits (breakfast, tea, cocktails) are called out as a meaningful perk across recent reviews
research_watchouts: Several 2024-2026 reviews flag dated decor in the lobby and some rooms, and inconsistent Club Lounge service on certain stays
The hotel is roughly 45-60 minutes from Suvarnabhumi Airport by car depending on traffic

faqs.question: What floor is the Vertigo restaurant on at Banyan Tree Bangkok?
faqs.answer: Vertigo and the adjoining Moon Bar sit on the 61st floor, an open-air rooftop restaurant and bar built on a converted helipad, giving diners 360-degree views across the Bangkok skyline that reviewers repeatedly single out as a genuine landmark experience rather than just a hotel amenity.

faqs.question: How many rooms does Banyan Tree Bangkok have?
faqs.answer: The hotel has 327 rooms and suites in total, spread across floors 15 through 58 of its 61-story Sathorn tower, with every category -- Horizon, Skyline, Panorama Club, Vertigo Club, and the multi-bedroom Serenity and Presidential Suites -- built to a suite-style, all-in-one-room layout.

faqs.question: When did Banyan Tree Bangkok open?
faqs.answer: It opened in January 2002 and has operated continuously since, making it one of Sathorn CBD's longest-running 5-star hotels; several 2024-2026 reviews note the lobby and some public areas read as dated relative to newer Bangkok luxury openings as a result.

reviews.title: Review: Banyan Tree hotel Bangkok (part of Accor) -- what do you get from £115 a night for a suite?
reviews.summary: Michele calls the suite-only rooms and Club Lounge strong value at the price, but flags a dated lobby, a small cold rooftop pool, and inconsistent lounge drink service.

reviews.title: Banyan Tree Bangkok review
